company.name: Verdant Roots Landscaping
company.summary: Verdant Roots Landscaping is a gardening and grounds maintenance company near Brisbane, Australia. You quote new garden projects, schedule field crews, run recurring maintenance contracts, invoice customers, and collect job photos. Your team is mostly field crews with a small office group handling sales, scheduling, and accounts.
offerings: Outdoor paving, paths, and retaining walls
Green waste removal and site clean-up
company.customers: Homeowners, property managers, body corporates, schools, and small commercial sites around Brisbane and nearby suburbs.

strategy.executive_summary: Most of your 30 staff are on tools, so the real AI wins sit with your five office staff and four crew leaders, who currently move every enquiry, quote, and schedule change by hand. Agents can triage enquiries, draft quotes from your price list, chase sent quotes, handle wet-weather rescheduling, and send invoice reminders, all inside ServiceM8, Xero, and the email you already use. Start with quote handling and reminders, which are low risk and should save about 11 hours a week in the first month. Across all three phases, expect roughly 25 to 30 hours back per week, worth around $30,000 a year in loaded wages, without changing how your crews work on site.

maturity.label: Digitised but manual
maturity.note: You already run ServiceM8, Xero, and mobile job apps, but the connections between them are people re-typing and forwarding. That makes your first automations cheap to set up, because the data is already in the cloud, it just never moves by itself.

opportunities.title: Quote enquiries answered in minutes
opportunities.description: An agent reads each new email or web enquiry, pulls out the address, job type, and photos, and creates a draft job in ServiceM8. It replies within minutes with your standard questions and an indicative price range, so your estimators spend time only on serious leads.
before: Check email through the day and note new enquiries
Call or email back for address, access, and details
Visit site to measure and photograph
Type up the quote from your price list
Send it and chase when you remember
after: Agent: logs the enquiry and drafts a reply with clarifying questions within minutes
Human: reviews and sends the reply
Human: visits site only for qualified jobs
Agent: assembles a quote draft from your price list
Human: checks the numbers and sends

opportunities.title: Wet-weather rescheduling without phone tag
opportunities.description: When rain stops work or a job runs long, the agent drafts a revised crew schedule, writes customer texts with new arrival windows, and updates job statuses in ServiceM8 for one-tap approval. A wet Brisbane week stops being a full day of phone calls.
before: Rain forces last-minute changes to the day's jobs
Call each crew leader with new instructions
Ring or text each affected customer one by one
Update job statuses in ServiceM8 by hand
Spend the afternoon sorting out confused callbacks
after: Human: marks the affected jobs in the app
Agent: proposes a revised schedule and drafts customer texts
Human: approves or edits with one tap
Agent: sends messages, updates statuses, and logs the change

opportunities.title: Routine customer questions handled without the phone
opportunities.description: An agent answers routine email and SMS questions like next visit date, rain delays, and invoice copies using live job data from ServiceM8. It also turns maintenance request emails, including customer photos, into draft jobs so nothing sits in the inbox overnight.
before: Answer the same questions by phone and email all day
Write down maintenance requests and retype them later
Upload customer photos to job records by hand
Requests that arrive after hours sit until someone checks the inbox
after: Agent: answers routine questions from live job data
Agent: converts request emails into draft jobs with photos attached
Human: handles calls and anything the agent is unsure about
Human: approves new jobs in ServiceM8

opportunities.title: No quote goes cold
opportunities.description: The agent tracks every quote you send, sends polite follow-ups on day 3 and day 7 using your templates, and flags anything silent after two weeks for a phone call. Your estimator gets a short weekly list of who to call instead of guessing.
before: Remember which quotes are still outstanding
Send follow-ups when there is spare time
Some quotes never get a second contact
Rebuild scope and pricing from scratch when customers finally reply
after: Agent: sends day 3 and day 7 follow-ups from your templates
Agent: records replies and updates quote status
Human: calls only the quotes the agent flags as cold
Human: revises scope with the customer when they re-engage

opportunities.title: Invoice reminders sent and queries answered
opportunities.description: The agent sends scheduled payment reminders from Xero and answers routine questions like invoice copies and bank details from your templates. Genuine disputes get flagged to you with a short summary so your bookkeeper only touches accounts that need a person.
before: Notice overdue invoices in Xero
Send reminders when the day allows
Answer repeated questions about copies and payment details
Chase disputed amounts by phone with no notes ready
after: Agent: sends reminders on your schedule and in your tone
Agent: answers routine invoice questions from templates
Agent: flags disputes with a one-paragraph summary
Human: calls the flagged accounts and settles disputes

opportunities.title: Job photos filed and attached automatically
opportunities.description: Crews keep taking photos on their phones as they do now, but an agent sorts them into the right job folder and attaches them to the ServiceM8 record, named by site and date. It checks each closed job and alerts the crew leader on the spot if before or after photos are missing.
before: Photos sit across a dozen phones
Crews upload or forward them at the depot
Office staff sort, rename, and attach them to jobs
Some jobs end up with no photo record at all
after: Human: takes photos as usual on the job
Agent: sorts, renames, and attaches photos to the right job
Agent: alerts the crew leader if a closed job has no photos
Human: reviews a weekly list of photo gaps

opportunities.title: Voice notes become job notes and timesheet checks
opportunities.description: Crew leaders send a 30-second voice note at the end of each job and the agent turns it into structured job notes, product use records, and flags such as a broken sprinkler or a customer complaint. Timesheet oddities get flagged to the scheduler before payroll, not after.
before: Fill in paper or app notes at the end of the day
Remember product quantities later or guess
Office re-keys details into records
Errors surface at payroll or on the invoice
after: Human: records a 30-second voice note at each job
Agent: writes structured notes and product records into ServiceM8
Agent: flags oddities like missing hours or unusual material use
Human: reviews flagged items only

opportunities.title: Plant and material orders drafted for you
opportunities.description: From each approved project the agent drafts a plant and material order against your supplier price lists, checks it for common misses like soil and mulch, and emails a draft to the nursery for your approval. Stage reminders to subcontractors for paving and irrigation go out automatically.
before: Build an order list from the approved plan
Look up prices across supplier lists
Email or phone each order in
Discover missing items mid-job and pay for return trips
after: Agent: drafts the order list from the job scope and price lists
Agent: emails draft orders to your suppliers
Human: checks quantities and approves
Agent: sends stage reminders to subcontractors

opportunities.title: Monday morning job profitability report
opportunities.description: The agent pulls invoiced amounts, labour hours, and material costs from Xero and ServiceM8 and writes a one-page Monday report ranking jobs by margin and flagging any that ran over estimate. You spend your review time on decisions instead of pulling numbers.
before: Export hours, invoices, and costs into a spreadsheet
Rebuild the weekly numbers by hand
Spot overruns days late
Chase crew leaders for explanations
after: Agent: compiles the one-page report by 9am Monday
Agent: flags jobs over budget with likely causes from job notes
Human: reviews and decides on pricing or crew changes
Human: questions crew leaders only about flagged jobs

roadmap.title: Office quick wins

Deploy the customer service inbox agent for routine questions and request logging

Draft plant and material orders for Garden Projects

risks.risk: A quote goes out with wrong prices or scope.
risks.mitigation: The agent drafts, a person checks and sends. Your price list stays the single source of truth and any price change needs approval.

risks.risk: Field crews ignore new steps and data quality suffers.
risks.mitigation: Crew-facing steps stay inside tools they already use, ServiceM8 and voice notes. Pilot with one crew leader and fix the friction before rolling out to everyone.

risks.risk: Customer photos, addresses, and payment details are exposed or misused.
risks.mitigation: Use Australian data hosting, restrict access to office roles, and set a written rule that customer data is never pasted into personal AI accounts.

risks.risk: Automated messages annoy customers or carry wrong information.
risks.mitigation: Every customer-facing schedule change and quote needs one-tap human approval. The agent drafts, your team sends.

risks.risk: Automations quietly break as prices, staff, or seasons change.
risks.mitigation: Book a monthly one-hour check with the consultant who set it up to update price lists, templates, and message rules.
